# Gestalt & Visual Perception

<!-- Generated by packages/rules/generate.mjs from data/laws/*.json. Do not edit by hand. -->

3 card(s). Check the code in front of you against each one that applies.

## GES-01 — Law of Proximity

- **Axiom:** Objects positioned close to one another are perceived as a unified conceptual group.
- **Apply when:** Form labels look attached to the wrong input, or unrelated actions read as one group because spacing is uniform.
- **Check:**
  - Place labels closer to their own input than to the preceding field (4px vs 24px).
  - Keep spacing inside a card tighter (8-12px) than spacing between cards (24-32px).
  - Group a primary action with its explanatory copy inside one layout cluster.
- **Instead of:** A form uses equal 16px margins everywhere, so each input visually attaches to the label below it.
- **Do:** Use 4px from label to input and 24px from the input container to the next field label.
- **Source:** Max Wertheimer (1923), *Untersuchungen zur Lehre von der Gestalt II*.

## GES-02 — Law of Similarity

- **Axiom:** Elements that share colour, shape, or size are read as one kind of thing.
- **Apply when:** Two different kinds of control share a style, or one kind is drawn three different ways.
- **Check:**
  - Give every primary action the same fill, radius, and weight; a variant is a different thing.
  - Draw metadata badges and filter pills in different shapes, not just different colours.
  - Reserve one accent colour for items that must stand apart from everything else.
  - Squint at a screen: if unlike things merge into blobs, the shared style is the defect.
- **Instead of:** Submit buttons appear as blue pills, green rectangles, and outlines on different screens.
- **Do:** All primary actions use one token: same background, text colour, radius, and weight.
- **Source:** Max Wertheimer (1923), *Untersuchungen zur Lehre von der Gestalt II*.

## GES-03 — Law of Common Region

- **Axiom:** A boundary drawn around things makes them one group, even when they are far apart.
- **Apply when:** A dashboard has no borders, so metrics read as one undifferentiated field.
- **Check:**
  - Put related fields inside one card surface with a single border or fill.
  - Keep at least 16px of padding inside a region so its contents read as contained.
  - Do not wrap every row in its own border; use a boundary only where grouping matters.
  - Test whether removing the boundary changes the grouping users report; if not, remove it. _(research: an experiment or a recorded run; not checkable from code)_
- **Instead of:** Thirty metrics sit on a bare canvas with only whitespace between them, so no one can tell which belong together.
- **Do:** Metrics sit in bordered cards with a faint background, each card holding one functional domain.
- **Source:** Stephen E. Palmer (1992), *Common region: A new principle of perceptual grouping*.
